r1_native_surface_for_comparison.meaning: hard re-entrant lengths on the undecimated R1 surface, from audit-20261110/mesh-audit.json native_voxel_surface

where_the_remaining_edges_are: R2a: 18 edges, all on the alternator's rear plane (y ≈ -5 mm) where it coincides with the fan cylinder's end, |x| <= 35 mm, z 232-244 mm. Sections show thin cusps there: blending the alternator rim alone pulls it off a plane the duct wall shares. R2b: 4 edges near x = +53, y ≈ -5, z ≈ 224 mm, where the alternator rim, that shared plane and the plenum top (z = 225 mm) meet; two pairwise blends do not round that three-surface corner. The location is measured; the cause is an inference from the sections.

verdict.reason: Neither R2 surface passes the unchanged rule of audit_mesh_admission.py: no re-entrant sharp edge at a hard junction and no crease off a constructive junction. Creases are 0 on both; R2a keeps 14.2 mm and R2b 8.0 mm of re-entrant sharp edge, against 1,089.5 mm on the undecimated R1 surface. The criterion was not relaxed.

not_run: no snappyHexMesh, blockMesh or checkMesh on either R2 surface: the gate before a mesh trial failed
no mesh-independence study and no flow solver
inspection: Sections at x = 0, x = 53 mm, y = -6 mm and z = 224/226 mm, and llvmpipe off-screen views of R1, R2a and R2b, were read on 2026-11-17. All three surfaces are closed, consistently wound single bodies. The blends sit only at the union seam and the alternator's rear end; nothing else moved. The images are not retained.
